title_en: How Will Less Fed Transparency Affect Markets and the Economy?
title_zh: 更少的美联储透明度，将如何影响市场与经济？
subtitle_zh: 三位前美联储理事与高盛首席经济学家谈 Warsh 治下美联储透明度下降的影响。
description: How Will Less Fed Transparency Affect Markets and the Economy?

turns.en: New Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh is steering the Fed into a less transparent era, with shorter post-meeting statements, less forward guidance, and a more limited role for projections.
turns.zh: 新任美联储主席 Kevin Warsh 正把美联储带入一个透明度更低的时代：会后声明更短、前瞻指引（forward guidance）更少，预测（projections）的作用也更有限。

turns.en: This marks a meaningful break from the transparency revolution that's defined at central banking over the last quarter century. So what might a less transparent Fed mean for markets and the economy?
turns.zh: 这是对过去四分之一个世纪里主导各国央行的那场透明度革命的一次实质性背离。那么，一个更不透明的美联储，对市场和经济意味着什么？

turns.en: I'm Allison Nathan, and this is Goldman Sachs Exchanges. Each month I speak with investors, policymakers, and academics about the most pressing market moving issues for our top of my report from Goldman Sachs Research.
turns.zh: 我是 Allison Nathan，这里是 Goldman Sachs Exchanges。每个月我都会与投资人士、政策制定者和学者对谈当今最牵动市场的议题，内容都出自我们的 Goldman Sachs Research 报告。

turns.en: For our latest edition, I spoke with former Fed governors Donald Cohen and Stephen Myron, as well as Jan Hoxiest, Goldman Sachs' chief economist, and head of Goldman Sachs Research.
turns.zh: 最新一期里，我对谈了两位前美联储理事 Donald Kohn 和 Stephen Miran，以及 Goldman Sachs 首席经济学家、Goldman Sachs Research 负责人 Jan Hatzius。

turns.en: I started by asking Jan if the shift toward a less transparent Fed is a positive or negative development. I do think that the transparency revolution in central banking over the last 40 years or so has been a good thing.
turns.zh: 我先问 Jan：美联储转向更不透明，究竟是正面还是负面的发展？我认为，过去四十年左右各国央行的透明度革命，一直是一件好事。

turns.en: If you provide significant information about your reaction function as a central bank, you say, if we get this kind of data, then this is what we will want to do about it, then financial markets can anticipate what is going to happen from a policy perspective.
turns.zh: 如果你作为央行就自己的反应函数（reaction function）提供充分信息——也就是说，如果我们拿到这样的数据，那我们就打算这样应对——那么金融市场就能预判政策层面会发生什么。

turns.en: Your meeting is not until four weeks later or six weeks later, but you get surprising information. It gets incorporated in financial conditions, and then you basically have to decide whether to ratify that, but if markets have good information about what your reaction function is, what your objectives are, what you think the tools achieve, then you'll see faster monetary policy transmission in a way that you can always not ratify.
turns.zh: 你的会议还在四周或六周之后，但期间你收到了令人意外的信息。这些信息会被纳入金融条件，于是你基本上得决定是否去追认它。但如果市场对你的反应函数、你的目标、你认为工具能实现什么都有充分信息，你就会看到货币政策的传导更快，而且这种方式下你总是可以不去追认。

turns.en: That's always an option, and I think that's a great framework. I think it's worked extremely well over the last several decades. I think unwinding transparency about the reaction function, in my opinion, would be bad.
turns.zh: 那始终是一个选项，我认为那是个很棒的框架。过去几十年它运作得极为出色。我认为，把关于反应函数的透明度撤掉，在我看来会是坏事。

turns.en: There's a separate question about forward guidance about the path of the policy rate, and I think there the answer is more nuanced. Economists sometimes refer to so-called odyssey and forward guidance, but this is tied himself to the mast, and you basically commit yourself.
turns.zh: 这里还有一个单独的问题，就是关于政策利率路径的前瞻指引，我认为那里的答案更微妙。经济学家有时会提到所谓奥德赛式（Odyssean）前瞻指引，就是你把自己绑在桅杆上，基本上许下承诺。

turns.en: You say, here's what we're going to want to do, even if the data at some point down the road tell us that maybe we should do something else.
turns.zh: 你说：这就是我们打算做的，哪怕未来某个时候数据告诉我们也许该做别的。

turns.en: That doesn't make any sense under normal circumstances. It can make sense when you have the effective lower bound for short-term interest rates, but even then it's a debate.
turns.zh: 在正常情况下这毫无道理。它只有在短期利率处于有效下限（effective lower bound）时才说得通，但即便如此也是个争论。

turns.en: Then there's so-called Delphic Forward Guidance, the Oracle of Delphi, the policy output that is conditional on the economic data that comes in.
turns.zh: 然后是所谓德尔斐式（Delphic）前瞻指引，像德尔斐神谕那样，政策产出取决于随后公布的经济数据。

turns.en: That's more defensible, I think, even in normal times. To counter-argument this, market participants are going to think that what is actually supposedly Delphic is odyssey, but I actually like the way the Fed does this with the dot plot.
turns.zh: 我认为这种即使在平时也更有道理。反对的论点是，市场参与者会认为本应是德尔斐式的其实是奥德赛式的。但我其实喜欢美联储用点阵图（dot plot）来做的这套做法。

turns.en: The dot plot is not, in my opinion, strong forward guidance, not even strong Delphic forward guidance. It's just the views of the different FOMC participants that are implied by their economic expectations.
turns.zh: 点阵图在我看来并不是强前瞻指引，甚至算不上强德尔斐式前瞻指引。它只是各 FOMC 参与者经济预期所隐含的观点。

turns.en: I do think most sophisticated observers understand the conditional nature of the dots. I do think they view it mostly as information about where you would be if the economy evolves in the way that the Fed expects, which is also incorporated in the summary of economic projections.
turns.zh: 我确实认为，多数老练的观察者理解这些点的条件性质。我确实认为他们主要把它当作一种信息：如果经济按美联储预期的方式演变，利率会在哪里——这也包含在经济预测摘要（SEP，Summary of Economic Projections）里。

turns.en: They understand that if you get a move away from that, that the policy would also change. So I view this more as additional information about the reaction function.
turns.zh: 他们明白，如果走势偏离那个预期，政策也会随之改变。所以我把这更多看作关于反应函数的额外信息。

turns.en: Don Cohen agrees that it's important for the Fed to provide clarity on its reaction function. But he sympathizes with some of Washington's views about forward guidance and the dot plot.
turns.zh: Donald Kohn 同样认为美联储就自己的反应函数提供清晰度很重要。但他对 Warsh 主席关于前瞻指引和点阵图的一些看法，抱有一定同情。

turns.en: One thing that I've pointed to over a number of years now is the focus on the median forecast in the SEP, the economic projections of the FOMC participants.
turns.zh: 过去许多年我一直在指出的一点是，市场过分聚焦于 SEP 里 FOMC 参与者经济预测的中位数。

turns.en: That is a very weak indication of where the committee is when just one person shifting can shift that median. And I've seen that happen every once in a while, one or two people shifting and then the market reacts.
turns.zh: 中位数其实是一个反映委员会立场的很弱的指标——只要一个人转变，中位数就会移动。我时不时看到这样的情况：一两个人一变，市场就跟着反应。

turns.en: So it's crazy to focus on that median. I think more serious is the forward guidance issues. So here I have a little sympathy with Chairman Morse.
turns.zh: 所以死盯那个中位数是很荒唐的。我认为更严重的是前瞻指引的问题。在这里我对 Warsh 主席有点同情。

turns.en: His concern is the forward guidance, what are we going to do next is both constraining the committee and constraining the market reaction to incoming information.
turns.zh: 他的担忧是，前瞻指引——也就是"我们下一步要做什么"——既束缚了委员会，也束缚了市场对 incoming 信息的反应。

turns.en: And I think a good example where it constrained the committee with adverse consequences was coming out of COVID. So the forward guidance was we're going to hold rates at zero until we're at full employment almost no matter what the inflation rate is.
turns.zh: 我认为一个因为束缚委员会而造成不利后果的好例子，是疫情之后的那段。当时的前瞻指引是：我们要把利率按在零附近，直到实现充分就业，几乎不管通胀率是多少。

turns.en: And I think just looking at the structure of that forward guidance and what world is it okay to have at the highest a real rate of minus 2% at full employment.
turns.zh: 我认为，单看那条前瞻指引的结构——在充分就业时，实际利率最高达负 2%，这是什么样的世界？

turns.en: So I think that forward guidance was not well conceived. And I think it did constrain the committee, which is not to say that some guidance isn't helpful and at the zero lower bound maybe necessary.
turns.zh: 所以我认为那条前瞻指引构思得不好。我认为它确实束缚了委员会，但这并不是说某些指引没有帮助、在零下限（zero lower bound）时也许是必要的。

turns.en: When you get away from the zero lower bound, I think there's less need for guidance and you can always adjust policy. So I think forward guidance becomes much less helpful when you get away from the zero lower bound and I would be a reluctant user.
turns.zh: 当你走出零下限之后，我认为对指引的需求就没那么强，而且你总是可以调整政策。所以我认为，走出零下限后前瞻指引的有用性大大降低，我会是 reluctant 的使用者。

turns.en: Having said that, I think the problem right now with Chairman Morse is not giving forward guidance. That's fine. I don't know if it's helpful in these circumstances, but he refuses to talk about how the committee sees the economy evolving.
turns.zh: 话虽如此，我认为现在 Warsh 主席不给前瞻指引这件事是没问题的。我不知道在当前环境下这是否有帮助，但他拒绝谈论委员会如何看待经济的演变。

turns.en: And I think that's not helpful. I think explaining how the committee is thinking about the economy, what it's worried about is part of helping the markets be stabilizing rather than destabilizing.
turns.zh: 我认为那没有帮助。我认为，解释委员会如何思考经济、担心什么，正是帮助市场起到稳定而非破坏作用的一部分。

turns.en: And it's part of accountability. He's got a communications task force. I hope that one of the messages they give him is you need a narrative.
turns.zh: 这也是问责的一部分。他有一个沟通工作组（communications task force）。我希望他们给他的信息之一是：你需要一个叙事（narrative）。

turns.en: You need a story. You need to be able to say what's going on in part because if you're not saying what's going on, how do you know when things aren't happening the way you thought they were going to happen?
turns.zh: 你需要一个故事。你需要能够说清楚正在发生什么，部分原因是：如果你不说清楚正在发生什么，你又怎么知道事情没有按你以为的方式发展？

turns.en: So you're holding yourself accountable. Alan Greenspan, whom Chairman Morse says he wants to imitate in many respects, always had a story. And then when things weren't evolving the way he and the committee thought they would evolve, he could see the data weren't lining up and questioned.
turns.zh: 所以你在对自己问责。Alan Greenspan——Warsh 主席说想在很多方面效仿他——总是有一个故事。然后当事情没按他和委员会预想的方式演变时，他就能看到数据对不上，进而追问。

turns.en: So what's wrong? What's going on here? So I think the story, the narrative is really, really important. But Steve Myron is more supportive of Warsh's push for a less transparent Fed.
turns.zh: 到底哪里出了问题？这是怎么回事？所以我认为故事、叙事真的非常非常关键。不过 Steve Miran 对 Warsh 推动一个更不透明的美联储，更为支持。

turns.en: So Steve, do you view less transparency as a positive or a negative development? I view it as a positive development. In my view, forward guidance has dampened volatility in the short run, but the flip side of that is that it has increased in the long run.
turns.zh: 那么 Steve，你认为更少透明度是正面还是负面的发展？我把它看作正面的发展。在我看来，前瞻指引在短期内压低了波动，但另一面是它在长期抬高了波动。

turns.en: By telling the market exactly what the Fed is going to be doing over the next several meetings or several quarters, the Fed reduced the sensitivity of financial markets to data that was coming in because the data wouldn't really matter that much because the Fed told you what they were going to do.
turns.zh: 通过精确告诉市场美联储在未来几次会议或几个季度里将要做什么，美联储降低了金融市场对 incoming 数据的敏感性，因为数据其实没那么重要了——反正美联储已经告诉你它要做什么。

turns.en: But at the same time, it resulted in two elements of greater volatility over the long run. One is that it increased the likelihood that the Fed would be behind the curve because it makes it too slow to adapt to changing conditions.
turns.zh: 但与此同时，它导致了长期内波动加大的两个方面。一是它增加了美联储落后于曲线（behind the curve）的可能性，因为它让反应变得太慢、跟不上形势变化。

turns.en: And so one thing that you saw at the end of the post-COVID experience was that the Fed was still buying mortgages when home prices were up 20%.
turns.zh: 所以你在疫情之后的末段看到的一件事就是：房价已经涨了 20%，美联储还在买抵押贷款（mortgages）。

turns.en: Why was the Fed buying mortgages when home prices were up 20%? I don't think there's a really good economic reason for doing so. I think a lot of it has to do with the fact that they said they would.
turns.zh: 为什么房价涨了 20% 美联储还在买抵押贷款？我不认为有什么真正好的经济理由这样做。我认为很大程度上是因为他们说过会这么做。

turns.en: They gave calendar-based guidance for their activities, and that resulted in them injecting credit into the housing sector very long after it was appropriate to do so.
turns.zh: 他们为自己的行动给出了基于日历（calendar-based）的指引，结果就是在远远不该的时候，仍在向房地产板块注入信贷。

turns.en: And the result of that inflation in the housing sector, I think, was pretty plain. So that was a very clear mistake that, in my mind, it was a result of forward guidance.
turns.zh: 我认为由此带来的房地产板块通胀是很明显的。所以那是一个再清楚不过的错误，在我看来，正是前瞻指引造成的。

turns.en: Another element to that is that I think it makes the market less good at pricing risks because the market will listen to the Fed as an indication of what's going to occur.
turns.zh: 另一个方面是，我认为这让市场对风险定价的能力变差，因为市场会把美联储当作即将发生什么的指示来听。

turns.en: And so if you take a look at Silicon Valley Bank, in my mind, there's no question about it that they were terrible risk managers. Part of the reason they were terrible risk managers is because they listened to the Fed.
turns.zh: 所以如果你看看 Silicon Valley Bank，在我看来毫无疑问他们是糟糕的风险管理者。他们之所以是糟糕的风险管理者，部分原因就是他们听信了美联储。

turns.en: The Fed said rates are going to be zero pretty much indefinitely, and therefore we can extend duration in our portfolios and take much more interest rate risk.
turns.zh: 美联储说利率将几乎无限期维持在零，因此我们可以拉长组合的久期（duration），承担更多的利率风险。

turns.en: When the government tells you something is going to happen, a lot of people tend to believe that. So I think that forward guidance really, although it appears to dampen volatility in the short run by making the market less sensitive to any given data release, I think in the long run you really manifest these really bad outcomes more frequently directly as a result.
turns.zh: 当政府告诉你某件事会发生时，很多人倾向于相信。所以我认为，前瞻指引虽然表面上通过让市场对任何一份数据发布变得不那么敏感而在短期压低了波动，但长期看，你其实会更频繁、更直接地招致这些糟糕的结果。

turns.en: But Steve, isn't there an important distinction between forward guidance in the sense of committing to a predetermined policy path, as you just spoke about, and the Fed being transparent about its reaction function?
turns.zh: 但 Steve，前瞻指引——像你刚才说的那样承诺一条预设的政策路径——与美联储就其反应函数保持透明之间，难道没有一个重要的区别吗？

turns.en: So in theory, there's a very big difference. In practice, I think the difference gets a little bit muddy because the data very often require interpretation.
turns.zh: 理论上，两者差别非常大。实践中，我认为这个区别会有点模糊，因为数据往往需要解读。

turns.en: For example, I can tell you the price of a barrel of oil because that exists, it's concrete. But inflation is the change to the general price level.
turns.zh: 比如说，我可以告诉你一桶油的价格，因为它是存在的、是具体的。但通胀是一般价格水平的变化。

turns.en: The general price level doesn't exist. It gets constructed by statisticians. And in constructing the general price level, there's 10,000 methodological choices that get made along the way.
turns.zh: 一般价格水平并不存在，它是由统计人员构造出来的。而在构造一般价格水平的过程中，一路上会做出成千上万个方法学上的选择。

turns.en: And to many of these questions, there's no objectively correct answer. So the truth is that the meaning of the inflation data changed a lot as a result of the way that these things are constructed.
turns.zh: 对其中很多问题，并没有客观正确的答案。所以事实是，通胀数据的含义会因为这些东西如何被构造而大幅改变。

turns.en: And sometimes there's a type of thing that monetary policy should respond to because they'd be persistent inflation that's a result of a supply demand imbalance that monetary policy can address.
turns.zh: 有时候，有些东西是货币政策应该回应的，因为那会是由供给-需求失衡造成、货币政策可以应对的持续性通胀。

turns.en: And sometimes they're not the type of thing that monetary policy should respond to, either because they're a one-off that you don't expect to be repeated or because they're a measurement error that you should just ignore.
turns.zh: 有时候，它们又不是货币政策应该回应的，要么因为那是一次性、不会重复的，要么因为那是你本该忽略的测量误差。

turns.en: So if you give too much transparency in the reaction function, then you run into situations in which you get a curveball from the data, and then you appear to be violating your reaction function or moving the goalpost.
turns.zh: 所以如果你在反应函数上给太多透明度，你就会遇到数据投来一个"曲线球"（curveball）的情形，然后你看起来像是在违背自己的反应函数、或者在移动球门柱。

turns.en: But look, I think you're right that there is a distinction between forward guidance in terms of telling people what you're going to do and forward guidance in terms of telling people what you care about.
turns.zh: 但是，我认为你说得对：告诉你打算做什么的那种前瞻指引，和告诉你你在乎什么的那种前瞻指引之间，是有区别的。

turns.en: I think that is an important distinction. And I do feel more strongly about the first than the second. So for example, when you think about the dots, do I think the dots need reform?
turns.zh: 我认为那是一个重要的区别。而且我对前者的感受比对后者更强烈。比如说，当你想到那些点时，我认为那些点需要改革吗？

turns.en: Absolutely. My view is the policy dot absolutely needs to go because as I said before, I think forward guidance increases the likelihood of large risk events.
turns.zh: 绝对需要。我的观点是，政策点（policy dot）绝对需要去掉，因为正如我之前所说，我认为前瞻指引会增加大型风险事件发生的可能性。

turns.en: I think the policy dot contributes to that. Markets and private sector agents should not be taking the Fed's indication of where policy is going when creating their own expectations for the future.
turns.zh: 我认为政策点加剧了这一点。市场和私营部门的参与者，在形成自己对未来的预期时，不应把美联储对政策走向的指示当作依据。

turns.en: The economic dots don't have as many downsides as the policy dots. So my view is the policy dot needs to go. But the other dots, I think that they're OK.
turns.zh: 经济点（economic dots）的缺点不像政策点那么多。所以我的观点是政策点需要去掉，但其他那些点，我认为没问题。

turns.en: But I think in general, you can narrow the presentation of guidance without necessarily getting rid of it altogether. Russians also argued that less transparency would allow markets to provide the Fed with more quote, direct and unfiltered end quote information about the economy.
turns.zh: 但总体上我认为，你可以缩小指引的呈现范围，而不必完全取消它。Warsh 还认为，更少的透明度会让市场向美联储提供"更直接、未经过滤"的关于经济的信息。

turns.en: I asked John whether he agrees. I disagree with that because markets price what they think the Fed will do, not what they think the Fed should do.
turns.zh: 我问 Jan 是否同意。我不同意，因为市场定价的是他们认为美联储会做什么，而不是他们认为美联储应该做什么。

turns.en: And that's not going to change if you obscure the Fed's reaction function. You're just going to have worse guesses on what the Fed will do, which would probably mean more volatility in rates markets and arguably broader financial conditions.
turns.zh: 如果你把美联储的反应函数弄模糊，这一点也不会改变。你只会得到对美联储将做什么更糟的猜测，这大概意味着利率市场波动更大，也可能波及更广的金融条件。

turns.en: And importantly, volatility that serves no good economic purpose. That's a really important distinction. Volatility per se isn't bad. If the outlook changes, then you would expect volatility.
turns.zh: 而且关键在于，那是一种没有任何经济用处的波动。这是一个非常重要的区别。波动本身并不坏。如果前景发生变化，你理应预期会有波动。

turns.en: You get massively stronger data. Yeah, of course, that should be a hawker shock. But if you just have less clarity about the reaction function, then market pricing is going to jump around more for not necessarily very good reasons.
turns.zh: 你得到明显强得多的数据——那当然应该是一个鹰派冲击（hawkish shock）。但如果只是反应函数的清晰度下降，市场定价就会因为并不是很好的理由而跳动更多。

turns.en: It also could mean that the moves that do occur just occur later. So it takes a longer time before monetary policy is transmitted effectively to the real economy.
turns.zh: 这也可能意味着真正发生的变动会推迟出现。于是货币政策要更长时间才能有效传导到实体经济。

turns.en: Don, for his part, sees a middle ground. I do think the Fed, being very specific about what it's going to do, could damp down the market's reactions.
turns.zh: 至于 Don，在他看来存在一个折中。我确实认为，美联储非常具体地说明自己打算做什么，可能会压制市场的反应。

turns.en: So if you say, well, I'm anticipating two interest rate decreases this year, but then the market gets some information that might suggest the rates should go up.
turns.zh: 比如说，如果你说"我预计今年会降息两次"，但随后市场得到一些暗示利率应该上调的信息。

turns.en: They might not build that in. So I think there's a golden mean here in which you give them some information. And this is perhaps what I'm thinking about with stories, narratives about what are you looking at without saying specifically what you're going to do.
turns.zh: 他们可能不会把它计入。所以我认为这里有一个"中庸之道"（golden mean）：你给他们一些信息——这也许就是我所说的，用故事、叙事去讲你在看什么，而不具体说你要做什么。

turns.en: And that will help the market process the new data coming in and free the market up to say, given what I know about the developing economic situation, given what I know about what you guys are looking at, here's what I think the path of rates needs to be for you to get to your price stability or your maximum employment objective.
turns.zh: 这会帮助市场消化 incoming 的新数据，让市场能够说出：鉴于我所了解的经济发展形势、鉴于我所了解的你们在看什么，我认为利率路径应该这样走，才能让你实现物价稳定或充分就业的目标。

turns.en: Don, if we presume that the outcome of less guidance is more short-term market volatility, is that a good thing or a bad thing? I mean, in other words, is that going to improve the signal or confuse the signal coming from markets?
turns.zh: Don，如果我们假设更少指引的结果是短期市场波动加大，那是好事还是坏事？换句话说，这会让来自市场的信号更清晰，还是更混乱？

turns.en: I think it could improve the signal. So if it is damped and we take off the damper but give markets enough information to react intelligently to whatever is happening, then a little volatility is fine.
turns.zh: 我认为它可能让信号更清晰。如果波动被压住了，我们把压制的盖子拿掉，但给市场足够的信息去对正在发生的任何事情做出明智反应，那么一点波动是没问题的。

turns.en: That's not awful unless you're creating a lot of uncertainty about where the economy is going, what your policy is aimed at. That's going to damp investment.
turns.zh: 这并不糟糕——除非你制造了大量关于经济去向、政策目标的不确定性。那会抑制投资。

turns.en: And so I think creating uncertainty for the sake of uncertainty is not a productive thing to do. That's another way of saying not telling the story is what creates volatility.
turns.zh: 所以我认为，为了不确定性而制造不确定性，不是件有建设性的事。这换个说法就是：不讲故事，才是制造波动的东西。

turns.en: So I do think there's something to be said for backing off from the specific guidance, but you need to help the markets figure out what the right path of rates is to accomplish your objectives.
turns.zh: 所以我的确认为，从具体指引上往后退一点是可取的，但你得帮助市场弄清楚，要实现你的目标，正确的利率路径是什么。

turns.en: And Steve Myron seems most convinced that reducing transparency would improve the market signal and says higher volatility is an unavoidable but ultimately acceptable cost.
turns.zh: 而 Steve Miran 似乎最为确信，降低透明度会改善市场信号，并认为更高的波动是不可避免但最终可以接受的代价。

turns.en: If you're getting forward guidance, there's very little volatility and there's no signal in the front end. It just reflects the forward guidance.
turns.zh: 如果你得到前瞻指引，那么短期端几乎没有波动，也没有信号，它只是反映前瞻指引。

turns.en: If you're not getting forward guidance, there's volatility and there's signal. And just because there's volatility doesn't mean that there's no signal, right?
turns.zh: 如果你没有得到前瞻指引，那么有波动，也有信号。而且仅仅因为有波动，并不意味着没有信号，对吧？

turns.en: Market behavior is always going to come with volatility. Markets will always be volatile, but if you hope to get any signal from the markets whatsoever, you have to accept that volatility.
turns.zh: 市场行为永远会伴随波动。市场永远会有波动，但如果你希望从市场得到任何信号，你就必须接受那种波动。

turns.en: The first best world of market signal without volatility doesn't exist. So you can't let perfection be your standard. There is no possible world in which you can get a strong market signal without volatility.
turns.zh: 一个既有市场信号又无波动的最优世界并不存在。所以你不能用完美当标准。不存在任何一个你能在没有波动的情况下得到强市场信号的可能世界。

turns.en: So you've got to accept the volatility along with the market signal. With so much at stake, I've then asked just how durable a less transparent Fed regime could be.
turns.zh: 所以你必须连同市场信号一起接受波动。既然利害攸关，我接着就问：一个更不透明的美联储体制，究竟能持续多久。以下是 Jan 的看法。

turns.en: Here's what Yon had to say. I think it's an open question. The chairman can, of course, make a lot of changes in terms of the regime. He controls what he says at the breast confidence, for example, that's something that nobody can take away from them.
turns.zh: 我认为这是个未解的问题。主席当然可以在体制上做出很多改变。比如，他在记者会（press conference）上说什么是他能控制的，那是没人能从他们手里夺走的。

turns.en: And if he wants to provide less information, then he can provide less information. So in that sense, it could be durable, but we'll see what the consequences are.
turns.zh: 如果他想提供更少的信息，他就能提供更少的信息。所以从这个意义上说，它可能持久，但我们拭目以待后果。

turns.en: The other question is, to what extent can a reduction in Fed communications broadly defined as, say, the number of speeches, how likely is that going to be durable?
turns.zh: 另一个问题是，美联储沟通的减少在多大程度上能持久——宽泛地说，比如演讲的数量。

turns.en: That's not going to likely be durable because I think the Reserve Bank presidents, you're not going to be able to shut them down. And they have strong incentives to continue to talk because that is their main role.
turns.zh: 我认为那不太可能持久，因为我认为储备银行（Reserve Bank）行长们，你没法把他们噤声。他们有很强的动机继续发声，因为那是他们的核心角色。

turns.en: And the boards of directors of the regional Federal Reserve Banks have a pretty strong incentive to have their presidents talk a lot. Increasingly, as a Reserve Bank, you are what your president brings to the table in terms of the monetary policy debate.
turns.zh: 各地区联储银行的董事会也都有很强的动机让自家行长多发声。如今作为一家储备银行，你在货币政策讨论中的分量，取决于行长能带来什么。

turns.en: So the cacophony could get worse if you have less centralized communication. A continued high level of talk from the Reserve Bank presidents.
turns.zh: 所以如果沟通更去中心化，嘈杂声可能会变大——储备银行行长们会继续高水平地发声。

turns.en: But Don views Warsh's current level of quietness as unsustainable. I don't think that the degree of quietness just from Chairman Warsh is sustainable.
turns.zh: 但 Don 认为 Warsh 目前这种沉默的程度是不可持续的。我不认为 Warsh 主席个人这种沉默程度能够持久。

turns.en: And I'm guessing that he knows that the July press conference was not a good look for Fed Chair. So you go through a press conference, short-term rates go down and long-term rates go up.
turns.zh: 我猜他知道，七月的记者会对美联储主席来说并不好看。一场记者会下来，短期利率降了，长期利率却涨了。

turns.en: So long-term rates are building in inflation or uncertainty premiums, risk premiums, term premiums. I'm sure that's not what he would have wanted going into the press conference.
turns.zh: 所以长期利率正在计入通胀或不确定性溢价、风险溢价、期限溢价。我很确定，这不是他在进入记者会时想要的结果。

turns.en: This is a very smart man. I worked very closely with him for nearly four years. Our offices were next to each other at the Fed. We worked hand in hand through the financial crisis.
turns.zh: 这是个非常聪明的人。我和他近距离共事过将近四年。我们在美联储的办公室紧挨着。我们并肩度过了金融危机。

turns.en: So I'm confident that Chairman Warsh recognizes that there's a void he needs to move in the direction of filling. I'm also confident that the communications task force will help move him in that direction.
turns.zh: 所以我确信 Warsh 主席认识到有一个空缺需要他去填补、需要朝这个方向推进。我也确信，沟通工作组会帮助他朝那个方向走。

turns.en: And while Steve believes that a sharp rise in volatility could force Warsh to rethink his strategy, he says we're far from that point today.
turns.zh: 而 Steve 认为，波动的急剧上升可能迫使 Warsh 重新思考他的策略，但他说我们今天还远没有到那一步。

turns.en: Steve, even if Chairman Warsh wants to have a quieter Fed, we all know that at some point volatility can get quite disruptive. So is there a threshold at which that volatility is just unsustainable?
turns.zh: Steve，即便 Warsh 主席想要一个更安静的美联储，我们都知道，波动到某个程度会变得非常具有破坏性。那么，是否存在一个阈值，超过它波动就变得无法持续？

turns.en: Absolutely. So let me go this way. A number of tools that were introduced in the GFC era, Ford guidance, QE, the formal inflation target, these are extraordinary tools for use at the zero lower bound when you are a creative deflation risk that you can't head off.
turns.zh: 当然有。让我这样来讲。金融危机（GFC）时期引入的一些工具——前瞻指引、量化宽松（QE）、正式的通胀目标——这些是为零下限时期准备的非常规工具，那时你面临无法化解的顽固通缩风险。

turns.en: In that environment, it is appropriate, in my view, to use those tools. But I have opposed these tools in 2009, 2010, no, I would not have. By the time you get to 2014, 2015, are they needed anymore?
turns.zh: 在那种环境下，我认为使用这些工具是恰当的。但我在 2009、2010 年并不支持这些工具——不，我不会支持。到了 2014、2015 年，它们还需要吗？

turns.en: Absolutely not. They all should have been repealed at that point completely. You use these tools when you need them. You take antibiotics when you're sick.
turns.zh: 完全不需要。那时它们全都应该彻底退出。你需要的时候才用这些工具，就像生病才吃抗生素。

turns.en: If you take antibiotics when you're not sick, you just create superbokes. And that's what we saw, I think, with the example before, where they didn't stop buying MBS.
turns.zh: 如果你没病也吃抗生素，你只会培养出超级细菌（superbugs）。我想前面那个例子就是如此——他们没有停止购买抵押贷款支持证券（MBS）。

turns.en: And so these tools, if you have an economic environment that suits them, are useful. But they become less useful outside of that economic environment.
turns.zh: 所以这些工具，如果你有一个适合它们的经济环境，是有用的。但在适合它们的经济环境之外，它们就没那么有用了。

turns.en: And their preciousness shouldn't be squandered. So if the increase in volatility is so much that it brings you back to the zero lower bound, you can offset it with lower funds rate.
turns.zh: 它们的珍贵之处不该被浪费。所以如果波动上升到把你重新推回零下限，你可以用更低的联邦基金利率来对冲。

turns.en: And sure, Ford guidance might be appropriate, but we're very, very far from that type of outcome. So with all of this in mind, we'll be closely watching how Fed communication evolves from here.
turns.zh: 那种情况下，前瞻指引也许就合适了，但我们离那种结果还非常非常远。所以带着这一切的考量，我们会密切关注美联储沟通从此如何演变。

turns.en: Let's leave it there for now. My thanks to Don Cohn, Steve Myron, and Jan Hotsias. And thank you for listening to this episode of Goldman Sachs Exchanges, which was accorded in August 2026.
turns.zh: 我们就先聊到这里。感谢 Don Kohn、Stephen Miran 和 Jan Hatzius。也感谢你收听本期 Goldman Sachs Exchanges，它录制于 2026 年 8 月。
